binders: A probability measure mu on Omega.
Two real-valued functions X and Y on Omega.
hypotheses: Finite branch: arbitrary real Holder-conjugate p,q with X in L^(ofReal p) and Y in L^(ofReal q).
First endpoint: X in L1 and Y in Linfinity.
Second endpoint: X in Linfinity and Y in L1.
conclusions: For each finite conjugate branch, |E_mu[XY]| is at most the product of the two integral moment roots.
At (1,infinity), |E_mu[XY]| is at most the real L1 norm of X times the real Linfinity norm of Y.
At (infinity,1), the analogous reversed endpoint bound holds.
mathematical_definitions: Expectation is the real integral with respect to mu.
Finite factors are written as integral moment roots.
MemLp combines almost-everywhere strong measurability with finite extended Lp norm.
Endpoint norms are eLpNorm values converted to real numbers.
HolderConjugate is the real Holder-conjugacy predicate.
translation.proposition_plain_english: On a probability space, the absolute expectation of XY is bounded by the product of conjugate Lp sizes, for finite conjugate exponents and both (1,infinity) endpoint orientations.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: Each branch is conditional on its own MemLp hypotheses.
The finite branch passes real exponents through ENNReal.ofReal; HolderConjugate is responsible for the positive admissible range.
MemLp makes the endpoint eLpNorm values finite before ENNReal.toReal is used.
The proposition assumes a probability measure.
ambiguities: The one-level dossier expansion reduces HolderConjugate to HolderTriple but does not display every primitive side condition.
Finite branches use explicit integral roots while endpoints use eLpNorm, so their common Lp interpretation is not syntactically uniform.
